abstract: We present matheshwara-v2026, a human model pre-trained on electronics and signals (one IEEE paper, one patent) and fine-tuned on machine learning at the University of Maryland. It specialises in grounded LLM systems: a clinical-triage assistant built at the Anthropic Hackathon, a stress-testing framework in which Claude reads Fed language to steer a stochastic rate model, and retrieval pipelines that keep patient data on the machine. As a data scientist at the UMD Counseling Center Research Unit, it co-authored a campus-wide study of food access and student well-being and an APA 2026 poster comparing ChatGPT with human researchers. This README is itself an experiment: an LLM agent writes its lab notebook every week, and a grounding check rejects anything it can't trace to real activity.

projects.name: Item-Item Collaborative Filtering
projects.question: How many neighbours does a book recommender actually need?
projects.method: Cosine-similarity KNN on a sparse item × user matrix, sweeping neighbourhood size and training ratio, global-mean cold-start fallback
projects.result: Best MAD 1.279 at k = 15; ratio sweep peaks at 0.85

projects.name: Local Medical RAG
projects.question: Can a medical Q&A bot be useful while patient data never leaves the machine?
projects.method: Ollama + Chroma + HuggingFace embeddings; intent routing for off-topic queries, a retrieval relevance threshold, stateful follow-ups; Dockerised
projects.result: Fully local pipeline: no third-party calls for protected health information

projects.name: Medical Chatbot on AWS
projects.question: What does it take to run a RAG chatbot in production, not just in a notebook?
projects.method: LangChain + Pinecone + GPT behind Flask; Docker image built by GitHub Actions, pushed to ECR and deployed to EC2
projects.result: Commit-to-container CI/CD path with conversation memory and LangSmith monitoring hooks

projects.name: Watt's Next?
projects.question: How far will the next EV go, and where should the chargers go?
projects.method: 216,772 Washington-state EV records: range regression, SMOTE-balanced incentive classification, clustering and geospatial analysis (co-authored)

projects.name: Sentimental Liquidity
projects.question: Can central-bank language move a stochastic rate model without letting the LLM become the model?
projects.method: Claude scores FOMC text for hawkishness (1–10) → bounded multiplier on the Vasicek mean-reversion speed → 1,000 Monte Carlo rate paths → logistic deposit-attrition model on 100k synthetic customers
projects.result: Net-interest-margin distribution with 90 / 95 / 99 % VaR and CVaR on a synthetic $10B deposit book

projects.name: TravelGenie
projects.question: Can one model coordinate many specialist tools to plan a whole trip from a single request?
projects.method: Claude orchestrates 7 MCP servers (flights, hotels, events, geocoding, weather, FX, traffic) behind Streamlit and Slack front ends
projects.result: One prompt → day-by-day itinerary with a budget breakdown (team project)

projects.name: ClinIQ
projects.question: Can a local LLM help an under-resourced clinic triage patients without inventing medical facts?
projects.method: Transparent rule-based severity score → llama3.1 (Ollama) clinical and plain-language summaries → strict RAG over ChromaDB (Gale Encyclopedia + openFDA labels) → 3-step prescription-safety check
projects.result: Built for the Anthropic Hackathon (Health & Wellbeing). Chat answers only from retrieved chunks; AI features disable themselves if the knowledge base is missing

projects.name: This profile
projects.question: Can an LLM agent keep this README current without hallucinating?
projects.method: Weekly GitHub Action: public activity → Claude (structured JSON) → grounding check on every repo name and number → one repair round → deterministic fallback
projects.result: Every published entry is traceable to the week's activity; figures are rendered from this repo's profile.toml

projects.name: Webpdf Scraper
projects.result: Crawls a site and extracts every linked PDF and PPT document

projects.name: Solar Flare Reporter
projects.result: Selenium scraper and analysis of NASA's top-50 solar flares

projects.name: Life-expectancy modelling
projects.result: Interaction-term regression on Gapminder with an F-test and residual diagnostics

projects.name: Bitcoin streaming
projects.result: Reactive price ingestion with Streamz; CoinGecko primary, CryptoCompare fallback, exponential backoff

chunks.text: We present matheshwara-v2026, a human model pre-trained on electronics and signals (one IEEE paper, one patent) and fine-tuned on machine learning at the University of Maryland. It specialises in grounded LLM systems: a clinical-triage assistant built at the Anthropic Hackathon, a stress-testing framework in which Claude reads Fed language to steer a stochastic rate model, and retrieval pipelines that keep patient data on the machine. As a data scientist at the UMD Counseling Center Research Unit, it co-authored a campus-wide study of food access and student well-being and an APA 2026 poster comparing ChatGPT with human researchers. This README is itself an experiment: an LLM agent writes its lab notebook every week, and a grounding check rejects anything it can't trace to real activity.
Pre-training: Electronics & signals: an IEEE UCMMT 2021 paper on D-band (160 GHz) traveling-wave-tube amplifiers and an IoT patent
Fine-tuning: Machine learning & data science at the University of Maryland

Deployment: Data Scientist, UMD Counseling Center Research Unit: campus-wide survey research on food access and student well-being, presented to the Vice President of Student Affairs and at the Maryland Student Affairs Conference
Specialisation: Grounded LLM systems: retrieval, tool-using agents, and LLMs as bounded signals inside quantitative models
Intended use: AI that has to be right: healthcare, finance, safety
Out of scope: Hallucinated medical advice. ClinIQ answers only from retrieved context
Eval highlights: R² 0.918 on EV range · MAD 1.279 on book ratings · 1,000-path Monte Carlo VaR / CVaR
Known limitations: Overfits to hard problems. Will refactor your notebook into a pipeline.
Status: Open to ML / AI engineering roles and research collaborations

chunks.source: Inductive bias · The LLM is a sensor, not the model
chunks.text: The LLM is a sensor, not the model. Claude returns one bounded score from Fed language; it shifts the Vasicek mean-reversion speed by −40 % to +50 %, and the SDE, Monte Carlo and VaR stay deterministic and auditable.

chunks.source: Inductive bias · Deterministic core, generative surface
chunks.text: Deterministic core, generative surface. Patients are ranked by a transparent point-based severity score; the LLM writes the summaries, never the ranking.
Fail closed. Every structured LLM call is parsed with fallback defaults; this profile's agent retries once, then falls back to a summary it can't get wrong.

chunks.source: Inductive bias · Sensitive data stays local
chunks.text: Sensitive data stays local. Medical Q&A runs on Ollama + Chroma on the machine, so protected health information never reaches a third party.

chunks.text: Specialists over a monolith. One orchestrating model, seven MCP servers, each owning exactly one job.
